retrieved_documents.body: ertugrul 1890. Description: 125 Years Memory (海難1890, Kainan 1890) is a 2015 drama film directed by Mitsutoshi Tanaka and written by Eriko Komatsu. A Japanese-Turkish co-production, the film was produced by Japan's Creators' Union and Toei together with Turkey's Böcek Yapım(tr). It was released in Japan by Toei on December 5, 2015, and in Turkey by Mars on December 25, 2015. The film connects two historical incidents that deepened the friendship between Japan and Turkey: The sinking of the Turkish frigate Ertuğrul off the Japanese coast in 1890, and the evacuation of Japanese nationals from Tehran in 1985. It received ten nominations at the 39th Japan Academy Film Prize, winning the awards for Best Art Direction and Best Sound Recording.
